items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: He wanted -- we were to be friends, his name was Merle Williams.

ctx.x: The story is that, if you want me to tell it from the beginning, my intention was to be a fighter. My father was a boxer. He was also a coal miner but he boxed around and he had taught me the pugilistic art. you know. And I was pretty good when I was a kid, when I was 5 or 6 years old. That was my intention because I used to buy all the literature on Jack Johnson, I had a whole scrapbook of him. And I was a Jack Dempsey fan. So I was going to be a fighter.

Across the street from me lived a fellow who was taking piano, he was about 11 and I was about 9 at the time. He wanted -- we were to be friends, his name was Merle Williams. M-e-r-l-e. He said to me, look, what do you want to be a fighter for? Why don't you play music. I said, you know, I never thought of that things. He said, well, come

on and study piano. He took me to his piano teacher, a lady named Josephine Guy, that's right. And I started studying piano and practicing on his piano because we didn't have a piano at home. I studied piano about a year and was doing pretty good. But the kids in the neighborhood started calling me a sissy because I was playing piano so I didn't want to play the piano, I gave it up. And one day Merle came over to my house and said, they're organizing a community band. And they're going to furnish the instruments…
